stem: Resources that are formed from the dead remains of living organisms over millions of years are called __________.
solution: Fossil fuels — coal, petroleum and natural gas — form from the remains of ancient organisms over millions of years.

stem: Natural resources that are present in unlimited quantity are called __________ resources.
solution: Inexhaustible resources like sunlight and air are available in unlimited amounts.

stem: Natural resources that are limited and will be exhausted by overuse are called __________ resources.
solution: Exhaustible resources like coal, petroleum and minerals are limited and can be used up.

stem: The slow process by which dead vegetation buried under the earth turned into coal is called __________.
solution: Carbonisation is the slow conversion of dead plants into coal under heat and pressure over ages.

stem: Coal was mainly formed from __________ that got buried millions of years ago.
solution: Coal formed from dense forests (plant matter) buried and compressed over millions of years.

stem: When coal is heated in the absence of air, it produces coke, coal tar and __________.
solution: Destructive distillation of coal gives coke, coal tar and coal gas.

stem: The almost pure form of carbon obtained from coal, used in making steel, is __________.
solution: Coke is a tough, porous, nearly pure carbon used in steel-making and to extract metals from ores.

stem: The black, thick liquid obtained from coal, used to make dyes, drugs and other products, is __________.
solution: Coal tar is a mixture of many substances used to make dyes, explosives, paints, drugs and more.

stem: Coal gas obtained during the processing of coal is used as a __________.
solution: Coal gas is used as a fuel, especially in industries located near coal-processing plants.

stem: Petroleum was formed from the dead remains of __________ that lived in the sea.
solution: Petroleum formed from the remains of tiny sea organisms buried under layers of sand and clay over ages.

stem: Petroleum is often called __________ because it is a dark, valuable liquid.
solution: Petroleum is called 'black gold' because of its dark colour and great value.

stem: The process of separating the useful components of petroleum in a refinery is called __________.
solution: Refining, done by fractional distillation, separates petroleum into useful products.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a product obtained from petroleum?
solution: Coke is obtained from coal; petrol, diesel and kerosene are obtained from petroleum.

stem: The fuel used in heavy vehicles like trucks and buses is __________.
solution: Diesel is used to power heavy motor vehicles, generators and pumps.

stem: The fuel used in light motor vehicles such as cars and two-wheelers is __________.
solution: Petrol is used as fuel in light vehicles like cars, scooters and motorcycles.

stem: The fuel used in stoves and lamps and earlier in aircraft (jet fuel) is derived from __________.
solution: Kerosene is used in stoves, lamps and as a base for jet fuel.

stem: The petroleum product used as fuel for cooking (in cylinders) is __________.
solution: LPG (liquefied petroleum gas) is used as cooking fuel in homes and industries.

stem: The slippery substances obtained from petroleum used to reduce friction in machines are __________.
solution: Lubricating oil from petroleum reduces friction between machine parts.

stem: The petroleum product used to make roads (paving material) is __________.
solution: Bitumen, a petroleum product, is used in paints and to make road surfaces.

stem: The raw material obtained from petroleum used to make many chemicals, plastics and fibres is called __________.
solution: Petrochemicals from petroleum are used to make detergents, plastics, synthetic fibres and many products.

stem: Natural gas is a __________ fuel that can be stored under high pressure as CNG.
solution: Natural gas is a cleaner fossil fuel; compressed under high pressure it becomes CNG.

stem: CNG (Compressed Natural Gas) is preferred as a vehicle fuel because it __________.
options: causes less pollution than petrol or diesel
solution: CNG burns cleanly, causing less air pollution than petrol or diesel.

stem: Natural gas can be transported over long distances easily through __________.
solution: Natural gas is conveniently transported through pipelines.

stem: Which of the following is a major advantage of natural gas as a fuel?
options: It is a cleaner fuel and can be used to make fertilisers and chemicals too
solution: Natural gas is clean-burning and also serves as a raw material for fertilisers and chemicals.

stem: Coal, petroleum and natural gas are __________ resources that must be used carefully.
solution: These fossil fuels are exhaustible and non-renewable, taking millions of years to form.

stem: Burning fossil fuels causes air pollution and releases __________, a greenhouse gas.
solution: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, contributing to global warming.

stem: The layers found in a petroleum deposit, from top to bottom, are usually __________.
options: natural gas, then oil (petroleum), then water
solution: In an oil trap, natural gas lies at the top, petroleum below it, and water at the bottom.

stem: The first oil well in the world was drilled in Pennsylvania (USA); in India, petroleum was first struck at __________.
solution: Digboi in Assam was the site of the first oil well in India.

stem: Which of the following is a way to conserve fossil fuels?
options: Using public transport and switching off unnecessary lights
solution: Using public transport, carpooling and saving electricity conserve fossil fuels.

stem: The advice by PCRA (Petroleum Conservation Research Association) to save fuel while driving includes __________.
options: maintaining a steady speed and correct tyre pressure
solution: Steady driving speed, proper tyre pressure and regular maintenance save fuel, per PCRA guidelines.

stem: The refining of petroleum separates its components based on their different __________.
solution: Fractional distillation separates petroleum components by their different boiling points.

stem: Which of the following is a renewable alternative to fossil fuels?
solution: Solar and wind energy are renewable alternatives to fossil fuels.

stem: The variety of coal that is nearly pure carbon and burns with the most heat is __________.
solution: Anthracite is the hardest coal with the highest carbon content and heat value.

stem: Coal is chiefly used to __________.
options: produce electricity (in thermal power plants) and in industries
solution: Coal is mainly used to generate electricity in thermal power plants and as an industrial fuel.

stem: The main reason to reduce our dependence on fossil fuels is that they __________.
solution: Fossil fuels are limited (non-renewable) and pollute the environment, so their use should be reduced.

stem: Which of the following statements about coke is correct?
options: It is used in the extraction of metals from their ores
It is used to make roads
solution: Coke, a nearly pure carbon from coal, is used to reduce metal ores in extraction (e.g., iron from iron ore).

stem: The process of forming petroleum and natural gas took __________.
solution: Petroleum and natural gas formed over millions of years from buried marine organisms.

stem: Which of the following pairs a fuel with its correct use?
options: Diesel – heavy vehicles; petrol – light vehicles
solution: Diesel powers heavy vehicles and petrol powers light vehicles.

stem: Which of the following is an inexhaustible natural resource?
solution: Sunlight is inexhaustible; the fossil fuels are exhaustible.

stem: Smoke from burning fossil fuels contains harmful gases such as __________.
solution: Burning fossil fuels emits sulphur dioxide, oxides of nitrogen and carbon monoxide, which pollute the air.

stem: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides released by burning fossil fuels can cause __________.
solution: These gases dissolve in rainwater to form acid rain, which harms plants, soil and buildings.

stem: The 'coal' that is the first stage of coal formation, still soft and with low carbon, is __________.
solution: Peat is the earliest, soft, low-carbon stage in the formation of coal.

stem: Which of the following would help reduce pollution and conserve fuel in cities?
solution: CNG public transport and carpooling reduce both pollution and fuel consumption.

stem: The dark coloured, thick, foul-smelling crude form of petroleum before refining is called __________.
solution: Crude oil is unrefined petroleum, later separated into useful products in a refinery.

stem: Which of the following is a solid fossil fuel?
solution: Coal is a solid fossil fuel; petroleum is liquid and natural gas/LPG are gaseous.

stem: A good fuel should ideally __________.
options: be cheap, readily available, produce much heat and cause little pollution
solution: An ideal fuel is cheap, available, gives high heat, is easy to store/transport and causes little pollution.

stem: Which of the following is a petroleum-based synthetic product?
solution: Plastics are made from petrochemicals derived from petroleum; cotton, wool and silk are natural.

stem: Which of the following correctly describes the environmental concern with fossil fuels?
options: Their burning increases greenhouse gases and causes global warming
solution: Burning fossil fuels raises greenhouse gas levels, driving global warming and climate change.

stem: Which of the following is the correct order of coal formation from the earliest stage?
solution: Coal forms in stages: peat, then lignite, bituminous, and finally anthracite (highest carbon).

stem: PCRA advises checking tyre pressure regularly because under-inflated tyres __________.
solution: Under-inflated tyres increase rolling resistance and fuel consumption; correct pressure saves fuel.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Coal and Petroleum' is that:
options: coal, petroleum and natural gas are exhaustible fossil fuels yielding many useful products, but they cause pollution and must be conserved
coal and petroleum have no uses
solution: The chapter explains the formation, products and uses of fossil fuels, and stresses that these exhaustible resources must be conserved and their pollution reduced.

stem: Coal, petroleum and natural gas are called __________ fuels.
solution: Coal, petroleum and natural gas are fossil fuels formed from ancient remains.

stem: Fossil fuels were formed from the remains of __________ over millions of years.
solution: Fossil fuels formed from the buried remains of dead plants and animals.

stem: Fossil fuels are __________ resources because they take millions of years to form.
solution: Fossil fuels are non-renewable (exhaustible) resources that will eventually run out.

stem: The process of heating coal in the absence of air to obtain coke, coal tar and coal gas is called __________.
solution: Destructive distillation of coal yields coke, coal tar and coal gas.

stem: The black, thick liquid obtained from coal, used to make dyes and explosives, is __________.
solution: Coal tar is a mixture used to make dyes, drugs, explosives and more.

stem: Petroleum is a dark, oily liquid found trapped between rocks below the __________.
solution: Petroleum is found deep beneath the Earth's surface trapped between rock layers.

stem: The process of separating the various components of petroleum is called __________.
solution: Refining separates petroleum into useful products by fractional distillation.

stem: The fuel used in aeroplanes is __________.
solution: Aviation fuel, a petroleum product, is used in aircraft.

stem: The petroleum product used for surfacing roads is __________.
solution: Bitumen, a petroleum product, is used for making roads.

stem: Natural gas is a __________ fuel that can be easily transported through pipelines.
solution: Natural gas is a relatively clean fossil fuel transported through pipelines.

stem: CNG, used in vehicles, stands for __________.
solution: CNG stands for Compressed Natural Gas, a cleaner vehicle fuel.

stem: Petroleum is called '__________' because of its great commercial importance.
solution: Petroleum is called 'black gold' because of its immense value.

stem: The process by which dead vegetation slowly changed into coal is called __________.
solution: Carbonisation is the slow process by which dead vegetation turned into coal.

stem: Coke is used mainly in the __________ of metals.
solution: Coke is used as a reducing agent in the extraction of metals like iron.

stem: The refining and separation of petroleum is carried out in a __________.
solution: Petroleum is refined in oil refineries.

stem: We should conserve fossil fuels because they are __________.
solution: Fossil fuels are limited and non-renewable, so they must be conserved.

stem: Burning fossil fuels releases gases that cause __________.
solution: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide and other pollutants, causing pollution and warming.

stem: The advice by the Petroleum Conservation Research Association to save fuel while driving includes __________.
options: driving at a constant, moderate speed
solution: Driving at a constant moderate speed and maintaining the vehicle saves fuel.

stem: The gaseous fuel obtained during the processing of coal is __________.
solution: Coal gas is a gaseous fuel obtained during the processing of coal.

stem: Which of these is a renewable source of energy?
solution: Solar energy is renewable; coal, petroleum and natural gas are non-renewable fossil fuels.

stem: The main gas present in natural gas is __________.
solution: Natural gas is mainly methane.

stem: Kerosene is used as a fuel for __________.
solution: Kerosene is used as fuel in stoves and lamps.

stem: The lubricating oil obtained from petroleum is used to __________.
solution: Lubricating oil reduces friction between moving machine parts.

stem: Using public transport instead of individual vehicles helps __________ fossil fuels.
solution: Public transport reduces fuel use per person, helping conserve fossil fuels.

stem: Petroleum and natural gas are usually found __________ in the Earth.
options: together, trapped above water in rock layers
solution: Petroleum and natural gas are found together, trapped in rock layers above water.

stem: The main reason fossil fuels should be used carefully is that their formation takes __________.
solution: Fossil fuels take millions of years to form and cannot be quickly replaced.
